focus: 全場都反對時守住你的判斷
lead: 今天練的是你是房間裡唯一反對的人時怎麼講話。心法：不要靠聲量，靠把你的懷疑變成一個可以被驗證的條件 —— 說清楚「要看到什麼我就收回」，最後就算輸了也要留下紀錄再走。每個 speaking 段落請先出聲講完再看 model answer。

phrases.en: Can I offer a different read on that?
phrases.gl: 我可以提出另一種解讀嗎？（不否定對方的數據，只質疑他的詮釋）
phrases.ex: Can I offer a different read on that? The overall number went up, but I think it went up in the wrong places.

phrases.en: I hear the argument, and I still land somewhere else.
phrases.gl: 我聽懂你的論點了，但我的結論還是不一樣（承認你有聽進去，同時不退讓）
phrases.ex: I hear the argument, and I still land somewhere else — I don't think one week of daytime data covers us.

phrases.en: What would change my mind is…
phrases.gl: 要讓我改變想法，需要看到 ——（把爭論變成一個具體條件，對方就沒得吵了）
phrases.ex: What would change my mind is a clean run on the night subset — give me that and I'll stop pushing.

phrases.en: I want to be the one voice of caution here.
phrases.gl: 我想在這裡當那個踩煞車的人（先承認自己是少數，反而讓人願意聽）
phrases.ex: Everyone in this room wants to ship, and I want to be the one voice of caution here.

phrases.en: Let's write down what we're each assuming.
phrases.gl: 我們把各自的假設寫下來（八成的爭執其實是假設不同，不是意見不同）
phrases.ex: Let's write down what we're each assuming — I think we disagree about how representative that night subset is, not about the model.
phrases.fix: 取代 “I think you misunderstand my point”

phrases.en: That's a decision, not a detail.
phrases.gl: 這是決策，不是小細節（阻止一個重要的事被順手帶過）
phrases.ex: Locking the threshold at 0.4 is a decision, not a detail — can we give it five more minutes?

phrases.en: Say more about why you'd rather not wait.
phrases.gl: 多說一點，為什麼你不想等？（用提問挖出對方真正的壓力來源）
phrases.ex: Say more about why you'd rather not wait two weeks — is something downstream depending on this date?

phrases.en: I'll go with it, but I want the risk on the record.
phrases.gl: 我配合這個決定，但風險要留下紀錄（輸得漂亮，而且保護自己）
phrases.ex: I'll go with it, but I want the night regression on the record in the review notes.

phrases.en: If I'm wrong about this, we'll know by the end of next week.
phrases.gl: 如果我判斷錯了，下週底就會知道（給你的擔心一個到期日，聽起來就不像唱衰）
phrases.ex: If I'm wrong about this, we'll know by the end of next week, when the second night batch lands.
phrases.fix: 取代 “I think maybe it will have problem later”

setup: Setup. It's the Wednesday model review, and the room is ready to sign off on the detection model for the next platform build. Alan's slide shows cut-in recall going from 0.81 to 0.87 overall, which is the best number the team has ever had. What bothers you is one line further down: on the night subset, recall actually dropped from 0.74 to 0.62, and that subset is only about 900 frames, so nobody trusts it enough to argue about it. David has already shown the 0.87 to the customer, and Grace wants the model frozen today so the labeling vendor can start on the next batch. You are the only person in the room asking to wait two weeks for the second night collection to land.

prompts.q: Alan: “Overall recall is up six points. You're the only one blocking this — what exactly is the concern?”
prompts.frame: Name the number you agree with → point at the one line that worries you → say why the small sample cuts both ways → state the condition that would change your mind → give it a date.
prompts.say: 先出聲講完整段（目標 40 秒），開場不要道歉，也不要用 “I think maybe”，再看 model answer。
prompts.model: “The 0.87 is real and I'm not arguing with it. Can I offer a different read on the rest? Overall recall went up six points, but night recall went from 0.74 down to 0.62, and night is where cut-ins actually hurt us. I know it's only 900 frames, and I know that's thin — but thin cuts both ways. It's not strong enough for me to call it a regression, and it's not strong enough for us to call it noise either. So here's what would change my mind: run the same checkpoint against the second night batch when it lands, and if night recall comes back above 0.74, I'll drop this completely. That's the end of next week, not two months. I'd rather spend eight days now than explain a night miss to the customer in October.”

prompts.q: David: “We went through this last week and we agreed to move forward. I don't want to relitigate it.”
prompts.frame: Accept that the discussion happened → say plainly what is new since then → keep it about the information, not about the decision → make a small, bounded ask → hand the call back to him.
prompts.say: 出聲練習「對比你資深的人堅持立場」—— 語氣要穩、要短，不要愈講愈小聲。
prompts.model: “Fair — and I'm not trying to reopen the whole decision. What's new is the night breakdown; we didn't have that split last week, we only had the overall number. I hear the argument for moving now, and I still land somewhere else on this one line. So let me make the smallest ask I can: freeze the model today as planned, but don't close the review item on night performance — leave it open with a check date of next Friday. That way Grace's vendor isn't blocked and we haven't quietly signed off on something we haven't looked at. If you'd still rather close it out today, that's your call and I'll follow it, but I want to say clearly that I think it's early.”

prompts.q: The room decides to ship. Grace: “So we're all good? I'll write it up as approved.” You lost — now close it well.
prompts.frame: Concede clearly, no sulking → ask for one specific line in the notes → name the trigger that would reopen it → offer to do the work yourself → end warm.
prompts.say: 出聲練習「輸了但不擺臉色」—— 不准說 “OK, whatever you decide”，也不要用嘆氣的語氣。
prompts.model: “Yes, we're good — go ahead and write it up as approved. One thing I'd ask for: put a line in the notes that night recall dropped to 0.62 on a 900-frame subset and that we're accepting that risk knowingly. Not to protect anyone, just so that if it shows up in October we know we saw it. And can we agree on a trigger — if night recall on the next batch comes in under 0.70, we reopen this rather than argue about whether to argue about it. I'll run that check myself the day the batch lands and send the numbers to the three of us. If I'm wrong about this, we'll know by the end of next week, and I'll be happy to be wrong.”

fixes.bad: We already discussed about this issue in the last review.
fixes.good: We already discussed this in the last review.
fixes.note: Transitive verb：discuss 後面直接接受詞，不加 about（同類還有 mention、explain someone something 的陷阱）。中文的「討論關於……」直譯過來就會多這個 about。

fixes.bad: Because the night subset is small, so the number is not reliable.
fixes.good: Because the night subset is small, the number isn't reliable.
fixes.note: Because…, so…：中文可以「因為……所以……」成對出現，英文只能留一個。留 because 或留 so，兩個一起用會讓母語者覺得句子沒寫完。

fixes.bad: We are running this evaluation since Monday and still no result.
fixes.good: We've been running this evaluation since Monday and we still don't have a result.
fixes.note: Tense：since + 時間點要搭現在完成進行式（have been -ing），表示「從那時到現在一直在做」。這是會議裡報進度最常出錯的一個時態。

fixes.bad: The night result is very very bad, I feel not good about this decision.
fixes.good: The night result is a lot worse — recall drops from 0.87 to 0.62, and that's what I'm uneasy about.
fixes.note: Intensifier + vagueness：very very 在英文裡聽起來很孩子氣，而且沒有資訊量。用數字取代情緒詞，你的反對才會被當成論點而不是情緒。

fixes.bad: Please kindly note that I have some concern regarding this decision.
fixes.good: I want to flag one concern before we lock this in.
fixes.note: Register：這是 email 罐頭語，講出口會像客服在念稿。口語用「動詞開頭 + 具體一件事」（I want to flag… / I'd push back on…），聽起來才像有立場的人。

challenge:
今天在真實會議裡做這一件事：當你是唯一反對的人，不要重複你的擔心，改成給一個驗證條件 ——

“Can I offer a different read on that? What would change my mind is ___. If I'm wrong about this, we'll know by ___.”

錄音作業（60 秒，手機錄）：挑一件這週你其實不同意、但沒說出口的事，用英文練一次。

  • 前 10 秒必須先講出你同意的那一部分（通常是對方的數字或目標）
  • 必須指出一件具體的事，不要一次列三個疑慮
  • 必須說出「要看到什麼我就收回」，而且附上一個日期
  • 最後 10 秒練一次「我輸了」的版本：接受決定 + 要求記錄風險 + 給重啟討論的條件
  • 禁用：very very、I think maybe、please kindly note、discuss about
check: 我今天反對的時候，有沒有先講出我同意的那一部分，再切進去？
我有沒有把我的擔心變成一個可驗證的條件和日期，而不是一直重複說我擔心？
決定不如我意的時候，我有沒有乾脆地接受，同時把風險留下紀錄？
